About Dydema
Dydema operates a platform for collecting and organizing human brain data. It brings together different types of brain and physiological data to support research and development in brain-computer interfaces. The company aims to make this data more accessible for researchers and developers working on brain-related technologies.
It was founded in 2025 and is based in San Francisco, California.

DYDEMA
03 About Y Combinator F26 Close Index (×) (↓)
We make the
brain buildable.
Dydema builds AI models that make sense of brain signals, and records the data to train them. Right now, building anything in neurotech means collecting your own data first. That’s where most ideas die. We do that part. Founded in 2025 and backed by Y Combinator.
Cajal / Histologie du système nerveux / 1909
why we started
Neurotech is short of data.
Language models learned from the whole internet. Brain models have almost nothing to learn from, because recording people is slow and expensive. So we build the models and record the data.
Julian

Julian does the neuroscience. He’s done every step of it himself, from fitting electrodes to training models, and he’s built organizations to do exactly that.

About Dydema
GPAgent's own fund-neutral profile, written from public information. Updated Sep 30, 2026.
Summary
The models handle signal interpretation that developers would otherwise have to build from scratch, and the data service fills a gap that currently limits the whole field. Together, they replace the need for neurotech teams to run their own data collection programs or build low-level signal-processing pipelines.
Business model
Developers access models via API and teams order custom brain recordings on request.
Go-to-market
Neurotech developers and research teams are the buyers; they reach Dydema's models through a developer portal and request data directly via the site.
